svg.text: Cross-linked through-rod cylinders replace the sway bar — resists body roll, stays compliant over single-wheel hits. Concept for hydraulic build review.
1 · MECHANICAL INTEGRATION — where the cylinders mount
• Cornering — chassis rolls, axle stays level → one cylinder compresses, the other extends → hydraulics resist.
• Heave (both wheels up together) → both cylinders stroke the same way → no differential → link is transparent.
• Single-wheel hit — axle tilts fast, like roll but momentary → the relief blows off so the wheel moves free.
Two double-rod (through-rod, equal-area) cylinders. Each cylinder's compression chamber is cross-piped to the OTHER cylinder's rebound chamber.
= the roll SPRING. Pre-charge sets roll stiffness;
one accumulator per circuit — symmetric for left & right roll
Through-rod cylinders keep displaced volume equal L↔R so the link stays honest. Roll cylinders are SEPARATE from the main coilovers/bypass (own circuit). Not to scale.
• Cylinders: double-rod (through-rod), equal area both ends so heave is volume-neutral.
• Cross-pipe: L-comp → R-reb, L-reb → R-comp. That single choice = heave-pass, roll-react.
• Accumulators: one per circuit. Volume + pre-charge set roll rate — the key tuning lever.
• Relief: bi-directional (hits come either side). Crack pressure = impact decouple point.
• Make-up: charged reservoir + checks for anti-cavitation and base pressure.
• Lines: short, large-bore, minimal restriction — flow lag kills the response.
• Discrimination is by duration: accumulator carries sustained roll, relief dumps brief
spikes. It is imperfect (a very fast turn-in can nibble the relief) — tune on a bench.
• Mounting: chassis brackets see real load — gusset to the cage, not sheet.
• Open items to size together: bore/stroke, accumulator volume & pre-charge,
relief crack & flow, line ID, bleed points, seal/fluid spec for desert heat.
• Could also run on the FRONT independent suspension — same circuit, per arm.
This attacks the RIGHT problem: roll-vs-compliance is the central
trophy-truck compromise, and interconnected hydraulics is real,
proven, top-tier tech (F1 heave, KDSS/Kinetic, Multimatic).
But it is NOT a magic bullet.
CG height, mass, power and tyre behaviour still rule stability.
This fixes one big lever, not all of them.
Build it as a bench-developed v2 — not the critical path.
Custom through-rod shocks + accumulator tuning + relief work is a
project that can stall the whole truck if it gates the build.
Get to Finke first on a light blade-adjustable bar + good bypass
valving. Race it. THEN chase this 2%.
Bench-prove the principle — two cylinders, an accumulator, an adjustable relief.
